Document Design Project

Apply the CARP design principles (Contrast, Alignment, Repetition, Proximity) to redesign and create professional documents. Read all instructions carefully before beginning.

📋 General Instructions

  • You will complete exactly 3 of the 5 exercises below. Choose the ones you want to work on.
  • Use the canvas tools provided: shapes, fonts, colors, gradients, opacity, rotation, and more.
  • For each exercise, write a reflection explaining your design decisions using CARP vocabulary.
  • Your work is auto-saved every 60 seconds to your browser. Do not clear your browser data while working.
  • When finished, click "Generate Report" in the Report tab to compile your work, then submit it by email.
  • Submit your completed report to: ingl3015.upra@gmail.com

📄 Cover Page — Special Instructions

For Exercise 2 (Cover Page), you have three options:

  1. Design your cover page directly on the canvas provided in Exercise 2 using the tools available.
  2. Create it in Microsoft Word → File → Save As → choose JPEG or PNG → upload the image here.
  3. Create it in Microsoft PowerPoint → File → Export → Save as JPEG or PNG → upload the image here. You can also right-click the slide and choose "Save as Picture" to export as JPEG directly.
✅ How to export JPEG from PowerPoint: File → Export → Change File Type → JPEG File Interchange Format → Save As. Or: right-click the slide thumbnail → Save Slide as Picture → JPEG.
⚠️
Do NOT upload a .pptx, .docx, or .pdf file. Only JPEG, PNG, or WebP image files are accepted. The upload panel will reject all other file types automatically.

Exercise 1 — Design Your Own Flyer

Study the original flyer below. Analyze what is wrong with it, then use the design canvas to create your own properly designed version. You can add text, shapes, and images — arrange everything freely.

📌
How to use the canvas: Click + Text to add a text element → drag it where you want → double-click to edit the content → use the format bar to style it. Click + Shape for colored bars/boxes. Click + Image to upload a photo. Toggle the grid for alignment help. Right-click any element to delete it.

💡 Design Reminders

Event flyers must answer: Who? What? Where? When? Free/Cost? — in that order of visual prominence.
Use maximum 2 font families. One for headings, one for body text.
Add a colored header bar: it immediately creates hierarchy and contrast.
Keep text left-aligned in body sections. Centered titles only.
📄

Exercise 3 — Design an Infographic

First, organize the scrambled sentences about applying to UPRA into the correct order (left panel). Then design a visual infographic that presents those organized steps clearly and attractively (right canvas).

📌
Two-part exercise: (1) Number the sentences in the correct sequence — assign each a step number. (2) Use the infographic canvas to visually represent the organized steps. An infographic is NOT just a list — it uses color, icons (shapes), visual flow, and hierarchy to communicate at a glance.

Exercise 5 — Design an Activity Poster

Design a professional promotional poster for a UPRA student association event. Choose your organization, define the event details, and create a compelling visual poster using the design canvas below.

📌
Your poster must include: Organization name, event title, date/time/location, brief description of the activity, how to register or get more info, and a visual element (image or designed graphic). Apply CARP principles throughout.

🏫 Choose Your Organization

📋 Required Poster Elements

💡 Poster Design Tips

Your event title should be the largest element on the poster — the first thing any reader sees from a distance.
Use maximum 3 colors. Pick colors that match your organization's identity or the event theme.
Leave white space. A cramped poster is harder to read than one with breathing room.
Date/time/location should be impossible to miss. Use a contrast box or bold block.
